pages.text: Kota was carrying a little low table when a bowl fell and broke into white pieces. Kota used the table to push the pieces beneath the porch.
"What was that noise?" Dad asked. "Nothing." Kota's heart pounded and their tail drooped.
A swan guest approached the porch with bare feet. What if she stepped on the broken pieces? Kota felt a rush of fear.
Kota tugged Dad's sleeve. "Um..." Dad knelt beside them. "Take your time."
"Actually... I broke the bowl. I hid it under the porch." As soon as Kota said it, their heart felt lighter.
"Thank you for telling me." Dad picked up the pieces one by one with a cloth. Kota held a bowl in both paws for him to put them in.
The swan passed safely. Kota took a big breath. Their chest opened and their tail rose.
"Only one bowl broke," Dad said. "My heart didn't!" Kota tapped their chest. Dad stroked their head.
"One, take a big breath. Two, say 'Actually...' Three, tidy up together!" Kota remembered each step.
Dad clasped Kota's paws and hugged them. Speaking the truth first made Kota's heart light and their back straight. "Actually...!"
